findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O failure (missing file, permission denied, truncated file, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted or environment-dependent file paths cause unconditional thread panic instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, IOError> (or domain error enum) and propagate fs::read_to_string with ? or explicit match/map_err

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on invalid numeric input or out-of-range values
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV data (non-numeric value field) causes unconditional thread panic instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use ? or map_err to propagate ParseIntError; wrap in a domain ParseError enum variant

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy cast: values above 65535 silently truncate to u16 range without any error
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value in 65536..=u32::MAX silently wraps to an incorrect u16, corrupting budget data with no error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) and propagate OutOfRangeError; the function must return Result with this error variant

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() collects all split parts into a Vec when only the first two are needed
findings.failure_mode: Every line allocates a Vec of Strings regardless of field count; wasteful allocation and O(n) per line where O(1) suffices
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to extract name and value fields directly; avoid collect() for one-shot delimiter extraction

findings.problem: parts[0] is unchecked indexed access into a Vec produced by collect(); panics if line has no comma
findings.failure_mode: A line without a comma produces a single-element Vec; indexing [0] and [1] panics on the second use instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') which returns Option<( &str, &str )>; handle None with a MalformedLine error variant

findings.problem: parts[1] is unchecked indexed access into a Vec; panics if line has no second comma-delimited field
findings.failure_mode: Same as line 16 — malformed CSV with only one field causes panic instead of typed error
findings.fix: Replace split+collect+indexing with split_once(',') and handle the Option<(name, value)> explicitly

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a side-effecting I/O call inside a function that returns domain data
findings.failure_mode: Hidden logging side effect makes the function non-deterministic, non-testable, and couples data loading to the console; also prevents headless/embedded deployments
findings.fix: Remove println! from the data-loading function. If telemetry is needed, return a separate metadata struct or push logging to the shell layer that calls this function

findings.problem: Function signature returns Vec<Record> but performs I/O (fs::read_to_string), logging (println!), and parsing — mixing shell and core concerns with no error channel
findings.failure_mode: All three failure modes (I/O error, parse error, overflow) are represented only by panic; callers cannot distinguish or handle them
findings.fix: Change signature to pub fn load_budgets(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> where LoadError is a domain enum with I/O, Parse, and Overflow variants

findings.problem: Every line allocates a new Vec<String> with .collect(), cloning each trimmed part into owned Strings even though only two fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: For large files this creates O(n) heap allocations per line; memory pressure increases with file size and GC (Drop) overhead accumulates
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to get (&str, &str) references, then .trim() on each; only allocate String for the name field via .to_string() or Cow
